subject: person alone
title: What If You Never Talked to Anyone Again?

scenes.text: What if you never talked to anyone again? Your brain would treat it like starving.
After just 10 hours alone, MIT brain scans showed people craving company the way hungry people crave food.
Over months, frequent loneliness more than doubles the chance of developing depression.
Over years, isolation raises heart disease risk about 29 percent, and stroke risk about 32 percent.
In older adults, long-term loneliness and isolation raise dementia risk by about 50 percent.
Add it up, and the US Surgeon General compares it to smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day.

description:
What if you never talked to anyone again? In an MIT study, 10 hours of isolation made the brain's substantia nigra respond to social images the way it responds to food after a 10-hour fast.
The 2023 US Surgeon General advisory links isolation and loneliness to more than double the risk of depression, about 29 percent higher heart disease risk, 32 percent higher stroke risk, roughly 50 percent higher dementia risk in older adults, and a mortality effect similar to smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: How long could you go without talking to a single person? Tag someone you would call first, and tell us what to test next.
